text:
blee: FYI - solace-ptq canary (streaming + kvcache reuse) is showing an unusual class of funcall parse failures where JSON objects are being split and stitched across stream boundaries. failing rate ~7.4% vs 0.9% fp16.

canary-bot: Canary alert: funcall_structured_parse_failure = 7.4% (5m) for solace-ptq-canary-1. dashboard: https://canary.internal/solace/ptq/1

tori: can we get one minimal raw concatenated stream sample? need to know whether it's a punctuation/token merge or an outright generation bug.

blee: pasted (joined streaming chunks):
```
[{"action":"batch_update","items":[{"id":11,"state":"ready"},
{"id":12,"state":"running"}]

{"action":"emit_event","args":{"topic":"jobs","k":2}}]
```
Note the first array never closed before a new top-level array/object started.

ram: that pattern suggests the model emitted a half-closed array then restarted an array/object. suspect quantization changed tokenization around punctuation (brackets, commas, whitespace). streaming + seq-packing seems to exacerbate it.

mika: novel thought: instead of blind bracket-cut heuristics, try a schema-anchored repair strategy: parse progressively using the JSON schema we expect for funcalls, prefer repairs that preserve the top-level action string and the types of args. Example: if schema expects an array of objects, we can try to close the last element rather than arbitrarily cutting at the last brace.

parser-lint-bot: Suggestion: emit these tags for each parse attempt: status=(ok|repaired|failed), repair_strategy=(cut|wrap|schema_anchor), repair_confidence=0-1, action_checksum_before, action_checksum_after.

benchbot: quick aggregated snapshot (n=500 multi-turn streaming sessions):
- fp16 baseline: parse_failures = 0.9%
- solace-ptq int8: parse_failures = 7.4%
- repaired (cut heuristic): 2.1%
- repaired (schema-anchored): 1.0%
- unrepaired: 4.3%
- repaired_but_action_changed: 0.4%

tori: interesting that schema-anchored gets fewer false-positive repairs. we should run an A/B of repair strategies. Also record the final token id sequence for failed sessions (last 12 tokens) so we can bisect at tokenizer level.

blee: one-shot mitigation: opt the canary traffic out of streaming for a small percentage (10%) and run the schema-anchored repair behind a feature flag for the rest. we should avoid auto-applying repairs for high-risk actions (delete, revoke, transfer).

ram: action: schedule a token-aligner bisect. plan: for a 1k-session synthetic probe, collect last-12 token ids for failed sessions under fp16 and ptq, compute token-id shifts around '[' '{' '}' ']' ',' and ':' tokens. if shifts correlate with failures, block ptq rollout.

mika: implementation note for schema-anchored repair:
1) attempt strict parse -> ok.
2) if fail, run tokenizer-aware scan to identify the deepest schema node that is complete (e.g., last valid array element).
3) attempt to close only the incomplete node (insert '}]' or ']' as required), validate against schema.
4) compute action_checksum_before (where available from partial parse heuristics) and after; if equal, accept with repair_confidence computed from fraction of tokens preserved and schema match score.

parser-lint-bot: Add telemetry event: funcall.parse.attempt with tags {model,quant,streaming,kvcache_reuse,batch_size,repair_strategy,repair_confidence,action_checksum_delta}.

tori: we also need a semantic safeguard: if repair_confidence < 0.7 but action_checksum preserved, mark as repaired_but_untrusted and surface a warning to the caller (dont auto-execute sensitive actions).

blee: bench plan: run 4x grid: streaming {on,off} x kvcache {reuse,no-reuse} with batch sizes {1,8} for 2k sessions, sample token-id dumps at 0.5% initially. compare cut vs schema_anchor repairs.

ram: dev tasks (quick assign):
- @mika: spike and PR schema-anchored-repair lib behind feature flag; emit repair_confidence + strategy tags.
- @tori: instrument token-id dumps to secure S3 with sampling and include model metadata; add parser telemetry event.
- @blee: run the grid and monitor repaired_but_action_changed metric; pause streaming ptq canary if unrepaired > 5% or repaired_but_action_changed > 1%.

mika: note - schema anchoring requires we ship a minimal schema for funcall outputs (top-level types and required fields). I'll add a small schema v1 in the flag.

tori: please also include a small synthetic bracket-probe test that intentionally emits nested arrays to stress the tokenizer boundary. that'll speed up bisect.

ram: medium-term: if bisect shows token-id shift for punctuation, either recalibrate PTQ tokenizer merges or disable seq-packing for streaming until we fix quant config.

benchbot: first grid batch done (250 sessions): schema_anchor repairs fixed 1.2% of sessions with 0 cases of action change. cut heuristic fixed 2.0% but introduced 2 action changes. Detailed dump uploaded to secure bucket.

blee: good first signal. keep schema-anchored on behind flag. Next update in this thread when the full grid finishes.

mika: tl;dr: solace-ptq streaming shows increased stitched/incomplete JSONs. short-term: schema-anchored repairs + telemetry + token-id dumps. medium-term: tokenizer bisect and PTQ config fix or rollback.

blee: thanks all. small ask: keep messages concise here and paste diffs/artifacts as links.
